questions.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{1}{s-5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{5t}} & =\frac{1}{s-5},\,s>5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{5t}} & =\frac{1}{s-5} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{e}^{5t}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-5}} \\ {e}^{5t} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-5}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-5}} & ={e}^{5t}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\frac{4}{3}{e}^{-2t}} & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{s+2}=\frac{4}{3s+6},\,s>-2.\end{aligned}

$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform of a Function Using the Addition Property
questions.worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{2{e}^{-8s}+{e}^{-5s}}{s}=\frac{2{e}^{-8s}}{s}+\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{u}_{8}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-8s}}{s},\,s>0 \\ L{{u}_{5}(t)} & =\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s},\,s>0,\end{aligned}
$$

where ${u}_{5}(t)=u(t-5)$ and ${u}_{8}(t)=u(t-8)$ are the unit step functions.

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{2{e}^{-8s}}{s}+\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-8s}}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{{e}^{-5s}}{s}} \\  & =2{u}_{8}(t)+{u}_{5}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{2{e}^{-8s}+{e}^{-5s}}{s}$ is $f(t)=2{u}_{8}(t)+{u}_{5}(t).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform of a Function Using the Addition Property
questions.worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{10+3{s}^{2}}{{s}^{3}}=\frac{10}{{s}^{3}}+\frac{3}{s}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{2}} & =\frac{2}{{s}^{3}},\,s>0, \\ L{1} & =\frac{1}{s},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{10}{{s}^{3}}+\frac{3}{s}} & =5{L}^{-1}{\frac{2}{{s}^{3}}}+3{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}} \\  & =5{t}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{10+3{s}^{2}}{{s}^{3}}$ is $f(t)=5{t}^{2}+3.$

questions.worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{6-5s}{{s}^{2}+9}=\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+9}-\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+9}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sin}⁡3t} & =\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0, \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{2}+9}-\frac{5s}{{s}^{2}+9}} & =2{L}^{-1}{\frac{3}{{s}^{2}+9}}-5{L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{6-5s}{{s}^{2}+9}$ is $f(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t-5\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{t} & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}},\,s>0, \\ L{{t}^{4}} & =\frac{24}{{s}^{5}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{8{s}^{3}-24}{{s}^{5}}$ is $f(t)=8t-{t}^{4}.$

questions.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{3!}{{s}^{3+1}}=\frac{6}{{s}^{4}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{6}{{s}^{4}} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{t}^{3}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {t}^{3} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} & ={t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4}\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}}={L}^{-1}{-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{-\frac{3}{2{s}^{4}}}=-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{9}{(s-4)(s+5)}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{9}{(s-4)(s+5)}=\frac{1}{s-4}-\frac{1}{s+5}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}} & =\frac{1}{s-4},\,s>4 \\ L{{e}^{-5t}} & =\frac{1}{s+5},\,s>-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-4}-\frac{1}{s+5}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-4}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+5}} \\  & ={e}^{4t}-{e}^{-5t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{9}{(s-4)(s+5)}$ is $f(t)={e}^{4t}-{e}^{-5t}.$

$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{3t}} & =\frac{1}{s-3},\,s>3 \\ L{{e}^{-3t}} & =\frac{1}{s+3},\,s>-3.\end{aligned}

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{6(s-3)}-\frac{1}{6(s+3)}} & =\frac{1}{6}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-3}}-\frac{1}{6}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}-9}$ is $f(t)=\frac{1}{6}{e}^{3t}-\frac{1}{6}{e}^{-3t}.$

$$

$$
